Tell me about your senior role at Novo

source: Tom's own account

Associate Product Director at Novo Nordisk (Feb 2022 - Feb 2026). Senior IC product role working across silos on complex, high-impact initiatives.

Work includes:

  • Consumer lead for the Wegovy Pill launch, driving prescription growth
  • Pitched and built a GenAI proof of concept for automating compliance reviews
  • Led a six-month discovery programme for the company's top drug asset, securing funding for a portfolio of digital initiatives
  • Introduced a digital incubation model that shifted the organisation from output to outcomes
  • Head of product operations. Helped product teams connect work to commercial outcomes.

Direct answers

  • CagriSema was the first drug to span two therapy areas, diabetes and obesity, that had never collaborated. Nobody had authority over both, so the discovery programme ran on influence.
  • The discovery funnel: 128 candidate ideas, a shortlist of 5, assumption-tested, 4 recommended and funded, each with a funding-gated rollout.
  • The organisational reflex was solution-first and siloed: output and theatre over outcomes. The incubation model was built to break that pattern.
  • Product Operations: standards, artefacts, ways of working. I know what good looks like because I've done it.
  • Digital Incubation: I established and led a digital product incubation unit, evaluating build, buy and partner solutions. It moved the business from solution-first to problem-first; CagriSema was its hardest test.
  • Head of Patient Products: led 6 experienced PMs building consumer engagement products, for a period, before moving into the pill team where the need was greatest. Management by outcomes.
  • Interim reorg of product teams before the Wegovy Pill project. Individual coaching and weekly experiment sharing; made individual product metrics public. Broke product silos, established weekly demos and experiment sharing, encouraged learning loops.
  • Given a wider remit to work across the product pipeline and complete the transition to a product operating model.
  • Established metrics across a diverse portfolio (12 products).
  • Built first cross-portfolio view of product team costs and capacity, started conversation around ROI.
  • Established product artefacts & quality standards across the product org, eg: gate model & deliverables, product-ops metrics, portfolio reports, business case templates, problem/north-star statements.
  • Mentored PMs to move from delivery-led outputs to commercial outcomes.
  • Secured funding, managed resourcing and cross-charges for incubation teams.
  • Designed portfolio model and gated incubation pipeline for branded digital engagement.
  • Shifted cross-functional VPs from product sceptics to advocates.
  • Chaired project steercos. Steercos were project management checklists: project not product focused, and unsuited for high-uncertainty discovery-stage products. Flipped the format from status updates to interactive co-creation, shifting cross-functional VPs from product sceptics to advocates.
  • Pitched 'Rybelsus Beyond The Pill' to Senior Management, an ambitious cross-functional pipeline for generating learnings & extending staytime. A small pilot is underway.
  • I lobbied Novo to switch sales data to a cohort retention model and failed.
  • Decisions won at executive level: the CagriSema discovery funnel, 4 recommended and funded, each with a funding-gated rollout, done without mandate[NOVO.R2]; 'Rybelsus Beyond The Pill' pitched to Senior Management, a small pilot is underway[NOVO.R2]; the final round job interview at Novo, where the business set aside its solution-first brief[NOVO.R1.TRANSFORM]; the TREAT recommendation to the board, which wound down the business[LEO.R1]; the GX Networks rename of a Plc, including the stock market ticker, in 5 weeks[HOST.R1.REBRAND].
  • The incubation unit was built through influence, with no formal mandate, and its discovery playbook was his[NOVO.R2].

Tell me about a GenAI project

source: Tom's own account

When developing health software, every release needs extensive regulatory review by medical, legal and regulatory experts (pharma calls it MLR). The process was designed for simple marketing materials, not sophisticated software - but it hadn't evolved.

In practice, every screen had to be captured in PDF format and reviewed individually. The result: significant delays (backlogs could mean months), huge documentation overhead, and an anti-pattern where you had to fully develop everything before getting sign-off.

I used an internal LLM sandbox to create a RAG model that captured the various guidelines and regulations. Now we could automatically document and review each submission with a full audit trail - the review team only had to rubber-stamp the release.

I also built a prototype agent that plugged into Figma, so designers could query the guidelines before investing too much effort. This allowed product teams to shift left - fail in design, not at review.

The product teams loved it. Organisational priorities later shifted and the project was handed to another team, but the proof of concept showed a clear path to dramatically faster release cycles.

Direct answers

  • Why it stopped at POC: it was built to test value, not to harden. Product teams used the Figma plugin on real designs and liked it, but a reorg and a vendor contract that covered the compliance-assistant use case meant it never got the second test or a path to production, and I moved on to the Wegovy Pill launch[NOVO.R2.WEGOVY]. Two tests were set; the first was run.
  • Rollout: the compliance RAG and the Figma agent were built for every product team's release review; the product teams loved it, and designers could query the guidelines in Figma, so teams could shift left; built the mandate to pitch for Generative AI regulatory reviews as a product and pitched senior leadership; execs weren't ready, and the project was handed to another team. Ways of working rolled out across organisations: design sprints, user testing and direct user interviews at LEO[LEO]; discovery, rapid prototyping and automated documentation at Novo, then a discovery playbook[NOVO.R1].
  • Dated: the agentic RAG compliance proof of concept was built in January 2025, inside the Associate Product Director role; two acceptance tests were set up front and the first was run with product teams on real designs[NOVO.R2.GENAI].

source: Tom's own account, direct answers
